This implies a potential role for Isoliquiritigenin in modulating the IFNAR signaling pathway, possibly through the enzyme's catalytic activity. The integration of these relationships highlights a possible regulatory interaction where Isoliquiritigenin may influence IFNAR function via the UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B15 enzyme. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Isoliquiritigenin and IFNAR, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
